Commentary.Commentary: Formats change but the bowler remains the same. It's Rashid Khan yet again for Afghanistan to do the damage. He became the first Afghan bowler to pick a Test fifer and has etched his name in the history books. The other bowlers also assisted him well as they finished the job. They though were a bit inconsistent in all the sessions today. Anyway, now it's up to their batters to achieve a historic win. Stay tuned for the chase...

Right then, Afghanistan need 147 runs to get off the mark in Test cricket. Once again their bowlers did an amazing job soon after Tea to remove both George Dockrell and Kevin O'Brien in quick succession. Although they will be disappointed as the last wicket stand once again frustrated them and pushed Ireland's lead close to 150. Earlier in the morning, Andy Balbirnie and James McCollum did brilliantly to put Ireland in a strong position, however their good work got undone post Lunch. Given the nature of the pitch, it's going to be an interesting finish to this Test match.

OUT! It is finally broken! Afghanistan can take a huge sigh of relief. They would have been frustrated surely though, Murtagh tries to pull this short ball and hit it for a six but the ball gets too high on him. It goes off the top edge of the bat and goes high instead of far. Rahmat Shah from deep mid-wicket comes running in, settles under the ball and takes a good catch to end the vital 58-run stand for the final wicket. Ireland end on 288, their second highest total in Tests, with a lead of 146.
FOUR! Slapped! A length ball on middle, Cameron Dow pulls it away through mid-wicket for a boundary and a widish long on cannot come around to stop it.
Bowled wide outside off, the batsman tries to put bat on ball after making room but cannot make contact.
Quick single taken this time! A short ball on middle, JCD stands tall and taps it onto the surface on the off side. A run is stolen as his partner responds quickly.
On a length on middle, James pats it towards cover and looks for a single but sensing the fielder is close to the ball, decides against it in the end.
Length ball on top of off stump, pushed towards the point fielder by Cameron Dow.
Floated delivery outside off, Murtagh looks to defend but gets beaten due to the drift on this one.
Tossed up on middle, Cameron Dow flicks it towards mid-wicket for a single.
Flighted delivery on off, James keeps it out.
Floated on middle, Murtagh flicks it towards square leg for a run.

50 up for the 10th wicket! Murtagh has again been involved in a handy partnership for the last wicket. But it's Cameron Dow who has done the major scoring this time. Coming to this delivery, it was bowled on the pads, James flicks it to the on side and goes for the single.
Full ball on off, driven straight to mid off and they take a run.
Defends this length ball off his front foot and into the ground.

FOUR! Murtagh is getting those handy runs for Ireland, be it off the edges or the middle. This one was on a length and outside off, Murtagh goes for the pull but gets a thick outside edge and the ball goes into the fence at third man.
FOUR! DRIVEN! Full ball on middle, Murtagh drives it straight down the ground. It is as straight as it could get. Boundary signaled.
Yorker ball on middle, Murtagh digs it out and places it to the off side.
Yamin Ahmadzai back into the attack.
Flighted delivery on middle, Murtagh drives it towards mid on for a run.
Floated delivery on leg, Cameron Dow nudges it towards square leg for a single.
FOUR! Nice shot. Tossed up on leg, Cameron Dow looks to sweep but gets a top edge. It goes wide of short fine leg for a boundary. These are crucial runs for the Irish team.
Full on off, Murtagh flicks it towards square leg for a single.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads.

FOUR! Edged! Lucky! Had there been a slip, he was a goner. Bowls a full, tossed up ball on off turning away, it takes the bottom edge of the bat and races away to the third man region. No fielder there to stop it.
Waqar Salamkheil is back.
Loopy delivery on middle, James nudges it to square leg.
Floated delivery on middle, Cameron Dow flicks it to the leg side.
Flighted delivery on middle, Cameron Dow nudges it to the leg side.

Fuller on the pads, flicked on the on side and a run taken.
Defends this one by getting right behind the ball.
Tossed up on leg and going down, Murtagh goes for the shot but misses. The keeper appeals for a catch but gets denied.
Full again on middle, Murtagh drives it towards mid on. The batsmen cross ends. 8 runs have come from the over. The lead is 109 runs.
250 up for Ireland. Full on middle, Cameron Dow drives it through mid on for a single.

Tossed up on off, Murtagh plays it towards point and sets off. There is a slight hesitation between both the batsmen. The fielder throws it at the bowler's end and the bowler tries to go for a direct hit but misses the stumps. Eventually, the batsmen get a run.

Flatter one on middle, pushed to deep mid-wicket for a single by the southpaw.
Hurled down the leg side, the batsman lets it go.

Tossed up on middle, Cameron Dow flicks it towards mid-wicket. The batsmen cross ends.
Short delivery, Murtagh pulls it through mid-wicket for a run.
Floated on middle, Tim defends it out.
Consecutive googlies from Rashid Khan. This is superb piece of bowling from the Afghan maestro. Floated outside off, Murtagh looks to defend but gets beaten due to the drift on this one.
Bowls a googly outside off, Murtagh looks to defend but misses it due to the spin on this one.
Beauty of a delivery. Turns away from the batsman, Murtagh looks to defend but gets beaten due to the drift on this one.

FOUR! Smashed! Missed it on the second ball but connects it well this time. Waqar bowls a similar delivery, James goes for the pull and gets it from the middle of the bat on this occasion. The ball races away to the deep mid-wicket fence.
Defends it off the front foot.
Excellent delivery! Waqar bowls it fuller in length and gets some away turn on it. Cameron Down strides forward in defense but misses it completely. The ball just misses his bat's outside edge.
Goes back on this full ball and defends it to the ground.
FOUR! Tossed on off turning in, James goes back and tries to pull but gets it from the inside edge of the bat and the ball runs away to the fine leg fence.
Full and on middle, pushed back straight to the bowler by the batsman.
Around the wicket for the last ball, Murtagh stands tall in his crease and defends this ball.
Just as I say beautiful bowling, Rashid sprays this one way down the leg side. The keeper fails to collect it and the ball lobs to short fine leg. No run taken though.

Oooh! Almost two in two! A googly on middle stump line and turning away from the lefty, Murtagh looks to defend the ball playing away from his body outside off. Takes the edge and just lands short of the slip fielder. Beautiful bowling!
Tim Murtagh, the hero of the first innings walks out to bat at number 11.

OUT! The replays also think the same! The foot is outside the crease when the bails were removed. The ninth one goes down! A googly from Rashid Khan landing on off stump line and turning away draws Andy McBrine to sweep. He misses the ball and in the process drags his foot outside the crease. The keeper, Ikram quickly collects the ball and whips the bails off. The square leg umpire signals for the third umpire to make the decision and the replays show us it is out. Rashid has his fifth! The first time for him and his country in Tests! Afghanistan have roared back after Tea just like they did after Lunch. The lead is 88 runs and just one wicket left now for the hosts to pick!
Stumping appeal... A googly from Rashid has drawn McBrine to sweep, Ikram has removed the bails and thinks that the batsman is outside the crease. What do the replays think?
Another one on middle and going through straight, Andy defends on his front foot but the ball goes off the inner half and almost carries to short leg.
Flatter one on the off stump, McBrine comes ahead and defends this ball.
Flighted outside off, Cameron Dow rocks back and puts it to the ground.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Cameron Dow has defended another tossed up delivery on his front foot presenting the full face of the bat.
Full on off, Cameron Dow prods forward and blocks it out.
Beaten! Cameron Dow goes back on a length ball and tries to punch it to the off side but fails to put bat on ball and it goes past the outside edge.
Floated ball outside off, defended showing the full face of the bat.
Around the wicket for the last delivery, bowled flatter and outside off. McBrine stays in the crease and keeps the ball out.
Flatter one landing on the off stump from over the wicket, defended by Andy coming ahead.
On the pads, worked away towards square leg for a single by Dow as he gets off the mark.
The googly first up! Dow has no idea and just hangs his bat to defend it off the back foot. The ball though turns away to beat the outside edge of the bat.
James Cameron Dow walks in at number 10.

OUT! Ireland's last hope departs! Rashid has caught O'Brien plumb in front here and he has set off on a run! This wicket is a massive one! A flatter one on middle and going straight on again instead of turning. KOB is caught on the back foot and he misses the ball. It goes on to hit the pads in front of the leg stump. The appeal comes and so does the finger. The ball might have just been clipping leg stump according to the replays. That doesn't matter now though, both the experienced men have been removed and Afghanistan are sensing a win here. That is also Rashid's 4th wicket in this innings!

Edged and FOUR! Flatter on middle, Kevin O'Brien looks to come ahead and defend but the ball skids on after landing and goes straight. The ball takes the inside edge and runs fine on the leg side for a boundary.
The second new ball is due now... but it has not been taken as yet. Rashid to continue.
FOUR! McBrine goes for a sweep on this full ball, gets it of the bottom edge of the bat. The ball rolls on to the vacant fine leg region.
Tossed up on off, driven straight to covers.
Big appeal for lbw, not given. It's a googly, McBrine is not able to pick that and is hit on the front pad after missing to connect. Replays show it was going down leg.
McBrine has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Bowls this one fuller and off, McBrine drives it uppishly straight to the cover fielder.
Starts off with a full ball outside off, punched towards covers for a single.
Salamkheil to bowl from the other end.

Huge appeal once more from Rashid, in fact he is celebrating but the umpire's finger remains in his pocket. A googly bowled outside the leg stump line and turning away to beat the outside edge of the southpaw who was ahead to defend. The ball goes on to hit the back pad of Andy in line of the middle stump but the umpire says not out because the ball was pitched outside leg. Good decision. End of a successful over for Afghanistan, a wicket maiden. The second new ball is due in 1 more over.
A flatter one on middle, Andy comes forward and keeps this out with the straight bat.

Loud appeal! Turned down this time. A flatter one landing on the leg stump line and turning inward. McBrine is ahead to defend but the ball beats his bat and goes to short leg who pouches it. There is an appeal for bat-pad but the umpire has seen there was no bat on that and hence, is unmoved.
Andy McBrine walks out next to bat.

OUT! A break in play and a break in concentration! The 63-run stand has been broken. Rashid strikes immediately after the interval. A flatter one on middle and going straight on instead of turning, Dockrell is caught on the back foot as he tries to flick it but misses. The ball raps him on the front pad just below the knee roll and the finger goes up. Looked like the ball would have been clipping the leg stump to the naked eye. This is a huge moment in the context of the game.
Defended onto the ground as the ball is flatter and outside off.
Flatter one outside off, turning away and left alone by Dockrell.

We are back for the final session. Kevin O'Brien and George Dockrell, the senior members of this Ireland team will look to continue the good work and increase the lead as much as possible. Meanwhile, Afghanistan will look to break this partnership soon as there might be some worries if the lead continues to swell. Rashid Khan, will try to do that as he has the ball in hand post the Tea break.
... Day 3, Session 3 ...

A session of two halves! One dominated by Afghanistan, another by Ireland. The Afghans made a roaring comeback post Lunch by nipping out four wickets in no time. With the visitors struggling, Kevin O'Brien and George Dockrell have come to their rescue and their unbeaten 63-run stand has put them 78 runs ahead of the virtual hosts. The bowling from Afghanistan was brilliant in the first hour but it dipped a bit in the second. The dropped catch of Kevin O'Brien has started to worry them now. The way this pitch has behaved, anything close to 150-175 is going to be daunting to chase. This match is interestingly poised. Which team will be smiling while leaving the field after the last session? Do join us in some time to find out.
Floated on off, O'Brien defends it out. THAT IS TEA ON DAY 3.

Short and outside off, Dockrell cuts it through point. The fielder chases it and stops it just before the ropes. He saves a run for the team. The batsmen take three runs. Good running between the wickets.

Huge shout for an lbw! Tossed up outside off, turning back in. Dockrell doesn't account for the excessive spin and offers no shot. He ends up wearing it on his pads and the Afghans let out a vociferous appeal. Nothing from the umpire. Mind you, he is not offering any shot. So impact is not in question. But it seems that the umpire feels that it will miss the sticks. The replays confirm the same.
Defended off the back foot to mid on.

Goes wide of the crease and delivers a good length ball on top of the off stump line, O'Brien punches it from the back foot to extra cover.
On a length on off, it's pushed from the crease to the off side but straight to the cover fielder.

50 partnership between Kevin O'Brien and George Dockrell. Floated on middle, Dockrell looks to defend but gets an inside edge onto the pads. It goes towards square leg for a run.
Flighted delivery on middle, Dockrell blocks it well.

Tossed up on middle, Dockrell defends it out.

Dockrell goes on the back foot and punches this to covers.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.

Bowls it on the pads, GD flicks on the on side and starts running. The mid-wicket fielder gives it a chase and stops it well inside the ropes. Three runs taken.
Full length ball outside off, driven straight to covers for a dot.

Flighted delivery on middle, Dockrell keeps it out.

Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

DROPPED! It was a sitter. Flighted delivery on middle, O'Brien looks to flick but gets an inside edge onto the pads. It goes towards short leg where Shahidi tries to take the catch but spills it.

Fuller in length, played straight back to the bowler.
Pitches this one a tad shorter and outside off, Dockrell punches it towards the cover fielder.
Tossed up delivery on off, defended off the front foot.

Drinks break. All the good work of the morning session by Ireland has completely been undone in the first-hour post Lunch. They lost wickets in a heap and slipped from 137/2 to 157/6 in a matter of seven overs and lost the plot. At effectively 37/6, all the Irish hopes are pinned on the shoulders of Kevin O'Brien and George Dockrell. Can Afghanistan finish things off in the next hour?

FOUR! Poor delivery from Ahmadzai. Full on leg, O'Brien flicks it towards fine leg for a boundary. Kevin O'Brien is scoring quick runs. The lead moves to 37 runs. This ball spoils a good over from Yamin Ahmadzai.
On a good length on middle, Kevin defends it off the front foot.
On a good length on middle, O'Brien defends it off the back foot.
On a good length and outside off, Dockrell plays it towards point for a run.
Length delivery outside off, O'Brien taps it to point.
Length delivery on middle, O'Brien flicks it towards square leg for a run.
Dockrell presents the full face of the bat and keeps it out.
Dockrell defends this tossed up delivery going on the front foot.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball.
Full ball onto the pads, O'Brien flicks it on the on side for a single.

BEAUTY! THAT'S A RIPPER! Leg spinner pitching on middle, O'Brien goes on the front foot to block this one but gets beaten all ends up. It turns away too much and Kevin has no clue about it. Rashid is bowling fire in his spell after Lunch.
Leg spinner pitching on leg, O'Brien blocks it well.
Dockrell offers a solid defense on this good length delivery.
On a good length on middle, Dockrell defends it off the back foot.
On a length and outside off, O'Brien plays it towards covers for a single.
Length delivery on middle, Kevin plays it to mid on.

Dockrell plays this ball presenting the full face of the bat.
Similar delivery, similar result.

Pitches it on leg, O'Brien clips it off his pads to the leg side and takes off for a single. The fielder at short mid-wicket hits the stumps at the non-striker's end. The ball goes to the off side and they come back for a second on the overthrow. The umpire takes it upstairs for a run out appeal but O'Brien was comfortably in. Not out flashed on the big screen!
Continues bowling from round the wicket and pitches it outside leg, O'Brien keep it to the off side.

Another one outside leg, Dockrell nudges it to mid-wicket for a single.

OUT! Thompson is out of here! Rashid strikes again. He continues from 'round the wicket angle for the southpaw and hurls in a flighted leg spinner outside off. Stuart stretches forward in defense but it spins back in big to beat his bat and strike him on the pads. They appeal vociferously and the umpire eventually raises his finger. Well, the impact looked outside the line there and also, maybe, there was some inside edge too. Is Thompson unlucky? Hang on. Some confusion over the mode of dismissal here. We are hearing that Stuart has been given out - caught at slip. So, there was some inside edge, which struck Thompson's pads and then lobbed up to Ihsanullah at first slip. Fair decision in the end. Ireland have lost the plot completely after Lunch.
Goes back and punches it to the off side.
Googly pitching way outside off, Thompson pokes at it but misses to put bat on ball.
Played through mid-wicket by the batsman.

Four byes! Leg spinner pitching outside off and coming way back in. Stuart tries to put bat on ball but the ball misses the bat and even the keeper's gloves and races away to the fence at fine leg. That went right through.
Flighted delivery on off, Thompson looks to defend but gets hit on the pads. The bowler appeals for lbw but the umpire is not interested. Replays show there was an inside edge on this one.

Floated on middle, O'Brien defends it off the back foot.

Flighted googly pitching on middle and going away, Stuart pokes at it but the ball goes past his outside edge and into the keeper's gloves.
Leg spinner on off, Thompson cuts it to point.

OUT! What a stunning catch at first slip! Afghanistan have turned things around post the Lunch break. Salamkheil serves a shortish ball just outside off, too close to cut but Poynter still goes for it from the crease. He gets a fat outside edge which travels at a rate of knots to first slip where Ihsanullah reacts quickly to grab a superb reflex catch. So after a century stand, it is going from bad to worse for the Irishmen.

Bowls wide outside off, O'Brien offers no shot.

LOUD APPEAL! NOT OUT! Rashid bowls this one on leg stump line, the ball hits Stuart on his pads and goes straight in the air to gully who takes a catch. Rashid first appealed for an LBW and then after that appealed for a caught behind. But the umpire shakes his head. Replays show no bat involved.
Leg spinner on middle, Poynter opens the face of the bat and guides it to short third man.
Floated delivery on off, Kevin keeps it out.
Full on off, Kevin drives it to covers.
Flighted delivery on off, O'Brien defends it off the back foot.
Floated delivery on middle, O'Brien nudges it towards fine leg. The batsmen pick up a couple.
Full on off, O'Brien drives it towards mid off.
FOUR! Wonderful shot. Full on off, O'Brien drives it beautifully through covers for a boundary. Ireland lead by 3 runs. They finally get into the lead.
Bowls it on off this time, Poynter moves forward and keeps it out.
Googly pitching on leg and turning in, Poynter moves across and lets it go behind his legs to the keeper.
Stuart Poynter is the new batsman in.

OUT! Plumb in front! One brings two and both the stars of the morning session are back in the hut in quick time. Rashid Khan dishes out a flatter delivery in the line of the stumps and gets it to skid off the surface. McCollum is caught on the back foot trying to hit across the line. Misses the ball completely and is thudded flush on the back leg. They appeal and the umpire agrees immediately. You cannot be more plumb than this. A fighting knock by the debutant is over too and Ireland are still to get into the lead.
Pitches it on middle, James rocks back and punches it to covers.
Another full ball, this time James defends it off the front foot.
Leg spinner pitching on middle, defended off the back foot.
Flighted delivery on off, O'Brien defends it off the back foot.
FOUR! First ball boundary for Kevin O'Brien. Cracking shot. Short and outside off, O'Brien makes room and cuts it through point for a boundary. Good way to get off the mark.
Kevin O'Brien is the new batsman in.

OUT! Here comes the breakthrough for Afghanistan after toiling hard. And it's a big wicket of the set batsman, Andy Balbirnie. Salamkheil bowled a few deliveries like this in the morning session too but without any success as it beat the outside edge then. Not this time though. He lands in a nicely tossed up ball outside off on a fuller length outside off. It kisses the turf and turns back in slightly as Andy leans into a cover drive. But he fails to middle his shot properly and edges it behind to the keeper. Ikram Ali Khil hangs on to a sharp catch and Balbirnie is seen walking without even waiting for the decision. A top knock by him but he will be disappointed to miss a century here. The deficit is still 5 runs.
Floated delivery on off, McCollum defends it towards third man for a run.
Tossed up on middle, Balbirnie flicks it towards mid-wicket for a single.
Full on off, Balbirnie drives it to covers.
Bowls it full and outside off, Andy prods forward and drives it to covers for a single. 7 from this over.
Strays on the pads and McCollum plays it to the on side. One run taken.
Goes on the front foot and keeps it out.
100-run partnership! Rashid bowls it full on middle, Balbirnie plays it with soft hands to mid on and scampers through for a quick run. This is only the second century stand for Ireland in Tests.
FOUR! Easy pickings. Bowls a full toss on middle, Andy plays a straight drive to the right of the bowler and the ball races to the long on fence.
Leg cutter outside off, Andy cuts it to backward point.
On off, James keeps it out.
Tossed up on off, Balbirnie plays it towards covers for a single.
Flighted delivery on middle, Andy defends it off the front foot.
Short and outside off, McCollum cuts it through backward point for a run.
Floated on off, Balbirnie punches it through point for a single.
Starts with a tossed up delivery on off, McCollum plays it with soft hands towards third man for a run.
We are back after Lunch. The players and umpires are out in the middle. Andy Balbirnie and James McCollum will continue their batting. Waqar Salamkheil will start the proceedings after Lunch.
... DAY 3, SESSION 2 ...

A good couple of hours in the morning session for Ireland! They did lose Paul Stirling courtesy an unfortunate decision but Andy Balbirnie and James McCollum have done exceedingly well post that to string in a crucial partnership. All thanks to their efforts, the deficit has now come down to 18 runs and Ireland will be feeling a lot more comfortable at the moment than they were at Stumps last evening. The Afghan bowlers, especially their spinners, were quite poor with their lengths and need to sort out their landing issues in the afternoon session. As of now, this Test match appears to be hanging in balance and let's wait and watch which way it turns after the break. Do join us in a short while.
Loopy delivery on off, James plays it towards wide mid on for a run. THAT IS LUNCH ON DAY 3.
Flighted delivery on middle, McCollum blocks it well.
BEATEN! Bowls a googly outside off, James looks to defend but misses as it spins past his bat at a quick speed.
Floated on off, McCollum looks to defend but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
Tossed up on off, James keeps it out.
Full toss and outside off, Balbirnie drives it through covers for a single.
And again... Action replay! Loopy and full, pitching wide outside off, James stretches out to defend but it spins back in and goes past the outside edge.
Mind games! Previous ball didn't turn but this one spins back in sharply from wide outside off. McCollum tries to defend by getting forward but once again is beaten.
Beaten! Tossed up ball landing outside off, McCollum hangs his bat out in defense but it skids past the outside edge.
Too full in length on off, it's pushed out off the front foot to covers.
Goes on the back foot and cuts it through point for a run.
Balbirnie has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Tossed up on off, James plays it to point. A better over from Rashid Khan.
APPEAL FOR CAUGHT BEHIND! NOT OUT! Full and outside off, McCollum looks to drive but misses it. Ikram Ali appeals but the umpire turns it down. Replays show there was no outside edge.
BEATEN! Beautiful delivery from Rashid Khan. Tossed up outside off, McCollum looks to defend but gets beaten due to the away turn on this one.
Bowls it short this time, James rocks back and plays it to the off side for a dot.
Tossed up outside off, defended off the front foot.

Edged but short of first slip! Rashid bowls a leg spinner pitching on off and turning just away to the right-hander who goes forward to defend it. The ball takes the edge of the bat and falls short of first slip. Had it carried then it would have been a happier Lunch for the Afghans.
Loopy delivery on off, James punches it towards point for a quick run.
Flighted delivery on off, the batsman keeps it out.
Floated outside off, James shoulders his arms to this one.
Outside off, McCollum leaves it alone.
Tossed up on off, McCollum blocks it off his front foot.
Full on off, Balbirnie drives it towards covers where Rashid Khan does a fine job to save runs for the team. The batsmen take a single.
Leg cutter this time outside off and turning away from the right-hander, James tries to poke at it but fails to get bat on ball.
Googly outside off and pitching short of a length, James leaves it alone.
Strays on the pads, Balbirnie works it to the on side and takes a single.
Leg spinner on off, Andy plays a square cut straight to point.
Andy leaves this full ball outside off straight to the keeper.
Bowls it short outside off, punched off the back foot to cover-point.
Flighted delivery on off, James blocks it off his back foot.
This was even better from Waqar. Slider outside off, James looks to drive but gets beaten as it skids on with the angle.
BEATEN! Bowls googly outside off, McCollum looks to defend but misses it due to the drift on this one.
Tossed up delivery on middle, James blocks it off his back foot. The ball kept low on him.
Floated delivery on off, McCollum defends it out.
Salamkheil comes from around the wicket. Bowls short and outside off, Balbirnie cuts it towards point for a single.
Another googly to Balbirnie who plays it off the back foot to cover-point and takes a run.
Googly on off, well read by the batsman. James goes in his crease and punches it to covers for a single.
Another short ball on middle, McCollum clips it to the on side.
Bowls it short and on off, James punches it off the back foot.
Tosses this one outside off, McCollum goes back and guides to the fielder at first slip.
Bowls a leg spinner pitching on leg, it's defended firmly by James.
Much better five balls after a boundary. Quicker and full on off, Balbirnie is on the back foot as he pushes it out safely to point.
Floated and full on off, turning back in, it's defended back to the bowler off the front foot.
A slider probably, around off and skidding away, Balbirnie sticks on the back foot in defense.
Lunges to a full ball on middle and works it with the spin to mid-wicket.
Quicker and flatter one, on middle and leg, Andy defends it off his pads to the on side.
FOUR! The poor bowling continues from the Afghan spinners. They have zero control over their length. Yet another long hop outside off has been smashed through point for a boundary.
Tossed up on middle, Balbirnie flicks it towards mid-wicket for a single. 7 runs came from the over. Suddenly, Rashid Khan is leaking runs.
Floated on off, James plays it towards point for a single.
FOUR! Good shot. Short and outside off, McCollum makes room and cuts it through point for a boundary.
Floated outside off, McCollum punches it to mid off.
Short and outside off, Balbirnie cuts it towards point for a single.
Flighted delivery on off, Balbirnie defends it off the front foot.

Excitement over a catch! Tossed up googly pitching on off to end the over. McCollum prods forward to defend it but misses it altogether. The ball goes past his outside edge and straight to the keeper who celebrates for a caught behind. Waqar starts to celebrate on his own but the umpire is unmoved.

Defends this full ball off the front foot.
Good running here from Ireland! Andy drives this tossed up ball straight to extra cover and goes for the single.
Changes the line and bowls it on off, it's played off the back foot to the off side.
FOUR! 100 up for Ireland! Starts up with a half-tracker outside off, Andy rocks back and cuts it hard towards the point region and the ball goes into the fence.

Bit more quicker on off, James defends it out.

Dot to finish. Andy defends this tossed up ball into the ground.

DRINKS! The first half of the morning session is over and apart from an unfortunate dismissal of Paul Stirling, it's been a decent going for Ireland. Afghanistan have also bowled well, maintaining tight lines but they would love to pick a few wickets in the next hour. 81 is the deficit now.

OUT! Given lbw! Stirling cannot believe his luck. He has a puzzled look on his face as he makes a long walk back to the pavilion. Here is what happened... Ahmadzai gets a shortish length ball to shape back into the right-hander from around off. Stirling tries to defend it with a straight bat but fails to do so properly. The ball raps him on the pads, the Afghans appeal and the finger goes up. Paul is bemused and the replays detect a BIG INSIDE EDGE. Nothing can be done now. No DRS for low-keyed sides. It's time to get going. The men concerned are out in the middle. Andy Balbirnie and Paul Stirling, two experienced blokes in the centre for Ireland, and they have to start well here and lead the fight. Deficit - 120. To wipe it off will be the first plan. Yamin Ahmadzai to kick off proceedings this morning with the ball. Here we go...

Pitch report - Ed Rainsford doing the pitch report says that the hardness of the new ball is posing more threat for the batsmen. Points out the area outside the left-hander's off stump. He says that it's dusty and breaking up. Also, he feels that runs can be scored on this surface if the batters apply themselves.

Hello and welcome back for the third day of this Test match between Afghanistan and Ireland in Dehradun. It's been a fast-paced game where the Afghans have got a firm grip. They bowled and batted better than the Irish boys to gain a handy lead, and going by the amount of wickets that have fallen on each day, this Test might end today itself. Can Ireland show some character and skill to infuse some life in their performance? Let's wait and find out...
... DAY 3, SESSION 1 ...

The Ireland's second sojourn started off on a very poor note as they lost their skipper on the very second ball. Andy Balbirnie and Paul Stirling though played out the remainder of the overs without any more wickets falling. The deficit is still 120 runs and the current pair will look to bat long on Day 3 if the visitors want to come back into the game. Meanwhile, a few early wickets for Afghanistan on Sunday will mean that the game is all but in their bag. What will happen? Join us on Sunday at 1000 local (0430 GMT) to find out! Till then, cheers and have a great Saturday!

When the day started, the away side would have still believed that they could have chances in the game. But all those thoughts were wiped off by a wicketless first session between Rahmat Shah and Hashmatullah Shahidi. They put up 130 runs between them before they were separated. Shahidi left soon after getting to fifty whereas Rahmat continued and fell agonizingly short of his ton. The batsmen who followed did not contribute much with the exception of Asghar Afghan who sent the Irish leather hunting with a quick 60-odd runs. The final few wickets though did not contribute much and Ireland restricted the lead to under 150.

An enthralling day of Test cricket comes to a close. One would have to believe that the Afghans will end the day with smiles. After batting most of the day and putting up a lead of 142 runs, they managed to scalp the important wicket of the Irish skipper and opening batsman William Porterfield. The lead is still a solid 120 runs and with the surface beginning to be conducive to spin, the 'hosts' are firm favorites in this Test.
Stirling goes on the back foot to play out the final delivery of the day. It was flighted and pitching on middle and defended to the on side. STUMPS ON DAY 2!

Punched off the back foot to covers. Two fielders run in to stop that. The batsmen steal a quick single.
Length ball outside off going away, Balbirnie poked at it but then left it alone.
Looped up ball to finish the over. Stirling taps it back to the bowler. 2 runs off the over.
Nabi gives air to this one. Stirling is not tempted to hit it and calmly blocks it off his front foot.
On the pads this time, Stirling glances it straight to the fielder at mid-wicket.
Loopy delivery on off and middle, Paul gets behind the line and blocks it.
Flighted delivery on off and middle, Stirling defends it.

Off spinner outside off, Stirling hits it towards point. The ball does not have the legs to reach the fence. Balbirnie looks for the third as the fielder gives it a chase but Stirling sends him back. Good call from Stirling there was never a three there.
Change of line from Ahmadzai. Bowls this outside off, Balbirnie shoulders his arms on that.
A length delivery on off, Balbirnie plays a perfect front foot defence on that.
Full length delivery outside off, left alone.
Full on middle and leg, played with a straight bat.
Pitched outside off, left alone.
A back of a length delivery on middle and leg, angling in for Balbirine who plays a loose shot towards short mid-wicket, but didn't carry to Rashid Khan.
Loopy delivery on the stumps, Stirling taps it back to the bowler to see off the over.
On middle and leg again from Nabi. Stirling glances it to the fielder at mid-wicket.
Off spinner pitching outside off, Stirling blocks it with a straight bat with minimal foot movement.
Lands it on middle and leg, Stirling tucks it to the fielder at mid-wicket.
On a length on middle and leg, Stirling gets on his back foot and blocks it.
Tossed up delivery outside off, Stirling brings out the sweep but hits it close to the fielder at short fine leg.
Well kept out by AB from the crease to end another disciplined over from Ahmadzai.
Another front foot defense from Andy to this one on a length outside off.
A length ball outside off, defended on the front foot by Balbirnie.
Stirling is off the mark! A nice push to this one on length outside off. The ball is to the right of extra cover. A quick single is taken.
Oooh! Nice shape but the line is wayward. The ball is delivered wide outside off and shapes away from the batsman who shoulders arms to it.
On a length on middle and leg, pushed back to mid on, off the front foot by Stirling.

FOUR! Risky shot from Balbirnie but gets the desired result. Shorter on off, Balbirnie waits for the ball to come and plays it very late, right under his eyes and cuts it through backward point for a boundary to finish off the over.
Loopy delivery on middle and leg, Andy glances it to the fielder at mid-wicket.
Full on off, Balbirnie does well to keep that one out.
Tossed up on middle, Andy flicks it to the fielder at mid-wicket.
Off spinner on off and middle, Balbirnie tucks it to the fielder at short leg.
Shorter in length on off, just a hint of spin on this one. Balbirnie blocks it.
Surprise, surprise! Mohammad Nabi to share the cherry.
On a length and middle stump line, pushed back down the ground to mid on.
Hurls this one on the pads, AB works it away to deep fine leg for a single to get himself and his team off the mark.
Well outside off this time, left alone by Andy.
On a length and middle stump line, pushed back to mid on by Balbirnie.

OUT! Up goes the finger and down goes the first one for Ireland. A peach from Ahmadzai. On a length, just outside off and Porterfield looks to defend the ball without foot movement. He gets a feather and Ikram takes a simple catch. Brilliant start for the hosts, not so good for the visitors. The new batsman at number 3 will be Andy Balbirnie.
Length ball outside off, left alone by Porterfield.
